messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager alert for customer GuardianHealth (VPC / dedicated pool). High 5xx rate and latency on model open-7b (tenant=guardian-prod). Alert started 2026-03-15T02:13:54Z. Severity: customer-impacting. @Ashley (oncall) assigned.

Ashley (oncall): Ack. I’m looking. Any quick context on traffic routing? Dedicated pool A, same region (us-west-2)?

Mike (SRE): Confirmed - traffic on guardian-prod is pinned to dedicated-pool-usw2-A. I'm seeing a sharp increase in KV cache misses and gRPC stream resets from the runtime nodes serving that pool.

Rami (Runtime Eng): Paging in. We deployed a small runtime patch ~90m ago that touched KV cache eviction heuristics for open-7b. Could be related. CPU on those replicas is normal but tail latency for decode is spiking. Logs show a lot of "kv_cache_lookup_timeout" around 02:12-02:14.

Ashley (oncall): Customer impact? Are requests failing or just slowed?

Mike (SRE): Both. ~18% 5xx (model backend errors) and p95 latency > 3s. Some requests are timing out before being retried. We’re seeing increased tail retry loops.

Sara (CSM): FYI I’ve opened a private thread with GuardianHealth support contact to let them know we’re investigating; they’re seeing errors in production and some billing-sensitive workflows affected. Please flag if we need to propose immediate mitigation.

Rami (Runtime Eng): My initial hypothesis: new eviction heuristics are aggressively purging large KV pages for open-7b in this workload leading to cold-KV thrash, which interacts poorly with our batching window and causes timeouts. A safe fast mitigation is to route GuardianHealth to the stable safe variant that uses a smaller KV footprint / quantized kernels: open-7b-stable-q4f.

Julia (PM): Do we have a rollback option for runtime change? If not, routing-level mitigation is preferred to avoid infra-wide rollback. Also need to consider model semantics differences for GuardianHealth. Sara, can you check whether the safe variant is acceptable functionally?

Sara (CSM): I asked Guardian support — they prefer a temporary fallback to a safe variant over a company-wide runtime rollback. They asked for as little behavior change as possible. They can accept a short-term quantized safe variant if we validate answer consistency for their top-5 prompt set.

Ashley (oncall): Plan proposal: 1) Pin guardian-prod tenant routing to open-7b-stable-q4f (dedicated pool) immediately for 100% traffic OR 2) Canary 20% to open-7b-stable-q4f, 80% to original, monitor for 5m, then promote. Which is safer?

Mike (SRE): Recommend option 2 (canary) to catch any regressive semantic differences quickly and avoid immediate customer churn. Also reduces blast radius if something else goes wrong. I’ll watch infra and metrics.

Rami (Runtime Eng): Agreed. I’ll stand up a temporary canary route and monitor KV miss rate and 5xx. Command to create routing override (admin CLI):

```
# pin 20% traffic for tenant guardian-prod to safe variant
redwoodctl routing create-override \
  --tenant guardian-prod \
  --from-model open-7b \
  --to-model open-7b-stable-q4f \
  --percent 20 \
  --pool dedicated-pool-usw2-A \
  --reason "emergency-vpc-eviction-thrash-2026-03-15"
```

Rami (Runtime Eng): I’ll push that now and report back.

OpsBot: deploy-bot triggered: routing override request queued (req-id: r-0a9c4). Approving via autosvc.

Rami (Runtime Eng): Override active. Canary started @ 02:20 UTC. Metrics baseline: p95 latency dropping, 5xx down from 18% -> 4% on canary. KV cache miss rate on canary nodes ~3x lower.

Mike (SRE): Looks promising. No new infra errors. I’m keeping alerts muted for canary traffic so we don’t double-pager. Monitoring dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/guardian-prod (sharing link).

Sara (CSM): Guardian contacts appreciate the quick mitigation. They asked for a note that we’ll keep canary for 30 minutes then either promote or roll back, and for a postmortem. I told them we’ll follow up with impact + root cause.

Julia (PM): Ok next steps: 30m canary, run 5 top-customer prompts through the safe variant to validate correctness. If metrics and prompt QA pass, promote to 100% for guardian-prod and schedule runtime revert during maintenance window. Rami, can you run the QA checks?

Rami (Runtime Eng): On it. I’ll run the customer prompt set against both models and diff tokens+logprobs. Quick results: top-5 prompt set shows token-level divergence < 1.2% and no critical hallucinations flagged by our eval heuristics.

Ashley (oncall): I’ll update incident checklist and prepare for handoff. Current status: canary healthy, mitigating customer errors. Paging suppressed for guardian-prod errors for next 15m while we observe.

Mike (SRE): Agree to promote if no regressions. I’ll stay on until promotion complete.

Sara (CSM): I’ll send Guardian a short update summarizing canary and next steps.

Rami (Runtime Eng): Promoting canary to 100% now. Command: `redwoodctl routing promote-override --req-id r-0a9c4 --percent 100`

OpsBot: routing override r-0a9c4 promoted to 100% at 02:48 UTC.

Mike (SRE): Post-promotion metrics: 5xx for guardian-prod dropped back to baseline (~0.8%), p95 latency back to expected. No new alerts.

Ashley (oncall): Summarizing for handoff: incident started 02:13 UTC with KV cache eviction-induced thrash after runtime heuristic change. Short-term mitigation: tenant-level routing canary -> promoted to 100% safe variant open-7b-stable-q4f for guardian-prod. Customer notified. Owners: Rami (runtime) to track root cause fix and runtime revert; Mike (SRE) to monitor infra; Sara (CSM) to coordinate customer comms; Julia (PM) to own postmortem.

Julia (PM): I’ll open the postmortem ticket and link the logs + eval diffs. Assigning follow-ups: runtime patch review + revert strategy (Rami), improved canary playbook for VPC tenants (Mike + Ashley), customer impact summary (Sara).

Ashley (oncall): Handoff to next oncall @ 03:14 UTC. If anything regresses, escalate to P1.

IncidentBot: Incident resolved (mitigation applied). Please add any missed notes and ensure postmortem is created.

Sara (CSM): Thanks team — GuardianHealth appreciated the fast mitigation. I’ll collate their feedback into the postmortem.
